messages:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT alert — increased 5xxs and node flapping in inference-pool-west-2. Metric spike at 18:09 UTC, multiple nodes entering NotReady. Paging oncall.
Maya (oncall): got it. looking at grafana: https://grafana.company.local/d/inf/pool-west-2 — CPU stable but GPU memory pressure + kubelet restarts visible. Assigning severity P1 for now.
Maya (oncall): quick summary: ~6/24 gpu-worker nodes NotReady; errors from runtime: `cuda: out of memory` and `kubelet: watchdog restart` in syslog on the affected nodes. Customers reporting higher latency and ~12% 5xx for text-generation endpoints.
Liam (eng-runtime): sharing runtime logs from one pod:
```
2026-03-15T18:07:11Z inference-runtime[pid=1234]: ERROR: cuda runtime: out of memory while allocating 512MB
2026-03-15T18:07:15Z inference-runtime[pid=1234]: process died, signal SIGKILL
```
Liam (eng-runtime): looks like process got OOM-killed then kubelet restarted the node's Kubelet service on some hosts (kubelet crashloop). Could be driver/driver + runtime memory leak.
Alex (infra): running `kubectl get nodes -o wide | grep NotReady` — listing affected nodes now: gpu-wn-07, gpu-wn-09, gpu-wn-13, gpu-wn-18, gpu-wn-22, gpu-wn-23. Host-level timestamps match kubelet restarts around 18:06-18:08 UTC.
Indra (sre): immediate mitigation plan:
- cordon NotReady nodes (they're effectively out, but cordon to be safe)
- create replacement nodes via autoscaler / scale group (ASG + image v3.2)
- restart kubelet on nodes that are NotReady but still reachable
- roll traffic to warm standby pool and enable failover routing for critical customers
Maya (oncall): executing commands now: `kubectl cordon gpu-wn-07 gpu-wn-09 gpu-wn-13 gpu-wn-18 gpu-wn-22 gpu-wn-23` — cordoned.
Alex (infra): triggering ASG scale-up + node reprovision: `infra-tool reprovision --pool inference-west-2 --count 6 --image v3.2` — provisioning new nodes, ETA ~5-7m.
Liam (eng-runtime): while new nodes come up, we can reduce model batch size and evict long-running KV-cache-heavy pods. Suggest `kubectl -n inference rollout restart ds/inference-runtime-gpu` to move pods to healthy nodes once available.
Maya (oncall): also applied routing override: `routing.set --pool inference-west-2 --fallback inference-cpu-global` for non-high-tier customers; high-tier still pinned to dedicated capacity unless they opt-in. This should cut 5xx noise for most tenants.
PagerDuty Bot: Incident acknowledged by Maya (oncall). Reminder: if customer SLA is impacted, escalate to SE.
Rachel (CS): FYI — I've opened an incident update for impacted customers and notified the two largest accounts. They want progress updates every 15 mins.
Indra (sre): trying soft-restart on kubelet for gpu-wn-13 and gpu-wn-18: `ssh root@gpu-wn-13 'journalctl -u kubelet -n 200'` shows repeated watchdog resets. Running `sudo systemctl restart kubelet` now.
Liam (eng-runtime): adding a check: please capture `dmesg | tail -n 200` and `nvidia-smi -q` before we fully recycle. Need to confirm if driver crashed or runaway allocation.
Maya (oncall): dmesg on gpu-wn-09 shows `oom_reaper: task inference-runtime invoked oom-killer`. Suspect memory leak in model KV cache path under high concurrent stream sessions.
Alex (infra): new nodes are starting, kube-proxy and kubelet healthy, now joining the cluster. 3/6 new nodes ready at 18:14 UTC.
Indra (sre): as nodes come back, we should `kubectl drain` the rebooted nodes with `--ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` to get pods scheduled to fresh hosts. Use caution for stateful pods.
Maya (oncall): Draining gpu-wn-07 -> success; pods rescheduled. Observed one pod crash on restart with exit code 137 (OOM). Killed pod had large pinned KV cache.
Liam (eng-runtime): temporary mitigations deployed:
- decreased default batch size from 8 -> 4 for affected model variants
- disabled long-lived KV cache for new sessions (opt-out flag)
- enabled aggressive auto-eviction of idle sessions after 30s
These reduce per-process GPU memory footprint.
Rachel (CS): customers acknowledged mitigations and appreciate the proactive routing. Asking for ETA on full recovery.
Alex (infra): cluster regained steady state: 24/24 nodes Ready at 18:21 UTC including the new replacements. kubelet restarts stopped. Node events quiet.
Maya (oncall): monitoring: 5xxs down from 12% -> 1.5% over last 10m; latency back to normal bands for most endpoints. Marking incident as mitigated but keeping the channel open for postmortem.
Indra (sre): next actions / follow-ups:
- collect full node logs and attach to incident ticket (kernel logs, kubelet, runtime)
- reproduce in staging with high-concurrency KV cache workload
- roll an engine patch with improved memory caps and OOM handling
- add node-level memory reservation to prevent kubelet crashloop
Liam (eng-runtime): I'll own the runtime patch and test in staging. Ticket created: INF-4832. ETA for hotfix: 48 hours.
Maya (oncall): handing off to Liam for overnight on-call. Liam — please take lead. I'll post a summary to #incidents and raise a postmortem ticket.
Liam (eng-runtime): taking it. Will follow up at 19:00 UTC with status and postmortem plan.
oncall-bot: Incident state changed -> Mitigated by Maya (oncall) at 18:22 UTC. Severity downgraded to P2 pending follow-ups.
Maya (oncall): thanks team — great triage. Filing postmortem stub and linking logs. Closing thread for now; keep me posted if anything reappears. :thumbsup:
